title: Enamel sexing of mammoth from Kostenki
projectDescription: We undertook the sexing of mammoth remains (n=21) from the russian site of Kostenki based on enamel protein characterisation. We use amelogenin, a protein that is expressed differently by amelogenin X and Y, depending on the coding gene it originates from (AMELX or AMELY).
sampleProcessingProtocol: Enamel was sampled from teeth of the 21 specimens included in the cohort. The enamel powders were immersed in 1 mL of 5%HCl and placed at 4Â°C overnight. HCl solutions were replaced the following morning after centrifugation and collection of the supernatants in S1 labelled tubes. Because demineralisation was not completed after the additional 12 hours at 4Â°C, all samples were placed at room temperature on a carousel to allow for complete removal of inorganic material for another set of 12 hours. After complete demineralisation, samples were centrifuged at 3000g for 10 min. Supernatants were collected into new microtubes, labelled S2, and placed in the freezer (-18Â°C) until further steps. Extracts were first separated by liquid chromatography on an Evosep One (Evosep, Odense, Denmark) using the â€œ60 samples per dayâ€� method with a gradient of 21 min for a total cycle of 24 min. Separation was conducted using a polymicro flexible fused silica capillary tubing (150 Âµm inner diameter, 16 cm long) home-pulled was packed with C18 bonded silica particles (1.9 Âµm diameter, ReproSil-Pur, C18-AQ, Dr. Maisch, Germany) with mobile phases consisting of A: 5% acetonitrile and 0.1% formic acid in H2O and B: 0.1% formic acid in H2O at a flow-rate of 2 ÂµL/min. The mass spectrometer, an Exploris 480 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) was set on data dependent acquisition mode with a first MS1 scan at resolution of 60 000 on the m/z range 350-1400. The twelve most intense monoisotopic precursors were selected, and were then dynamically excluded after one appearance with their isotopes (Â± 20 ppm) for 20 seconds. The selected peptides were acquired on MS2 at the Orbitrap resolving power of 15000, HCD set at 30%, quadrupole isolation width of 1.3 m/z and first m/z of 120.
dataProcessingProtocol: A protein reference database containing entries for 12 proteins (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL17A1, AMELX, AMELY, TUFT1, AMBN, AMLT, ALB, ENAM, ODAM, and MMP20) for Elephas maximus and Loxodonta africana derived from Genbank and UniProt was built prior to data processing.  Proteomic data analysis was conducted in Maxquant v. 2.1.3.0 using the following parameters: unspecific digestion; maximum of 5 variable PTMs (deamidation (NQ), phosphorylation (STY), and oxidation (MP)); peptides length set to be between 7 and 30 amino acids; minimum score of 40. False discovery rate for both peptides and proteins was set at 1%. Other settings were left as default.
